candidates.title: Toyota T-Connect access key exposed on public GitHub

discovery.usageRights: Citation and short paraphrase only; check publisher terms before reuse. Japanese-language notice; statements here are translated paraphrases.
Citation and short paraphrase only; check publisher terms before reuse.

candidates.dedupeCheck: No existing seed incident shares this identity.

claims.statement: A development subcontractor published part of the T-Connect website source code, including a data server access key, to a public GitHub repository in December 2017.
The repository stayed public until 15 September 2022, and the key was changed on 17 September 2022.

Toyota's notice (7 October 2022) says a T-Connect website development contractor uploaded part of the source code, including a data server access key, to a public GitHub repository in December 2017; it was accessible until 15 September 2022 and the key was changed on 17 September 2022.

Toyota says 296,019 customer email addresses and customer management numbers may have been exposed; third-party access could not be confirmed but could not be ruled out, and no misuse had been confirmed.

unresolvedQuestions: Whether the key was used is unknown; Toyota could not confirm or rule it out from access history.
CWE-798 (hard-coded credentials) is a weakness candidate only; not independently evidenced.

candidates.title: Okta support system breach exposing session tokens in HAR files

discovery.usageRights: Citation and short paraphrase only; check publisher terms before reuse.
Citation and short paraphrase only; check publisher terms before reuse.

candidates.dedupeCheck: No existing seed incident shares this identity.

claims.statement: An actor used a stolen credential to access Okta's support case system and view files customers uploaded to support cases.
Some of those HAR files contained cookies and session tokens.

Okta's root-cause report (3 November 2023) says the access used a service account whose username and password had been saved to an employee's personal Google account, most likely exposed through that personal account or device.
Between 28 September and 17 October 2023 the actor accessed files tied to 134 Okta customers; some were HAR files with session tokens, used to hijack the Okta sessions of 5 customers.

unresolvedQuestions: Okta first disclosed the incident on 20 October 2023 and closed its investigation on 8 February 2024 (sec.okta.com/harfiles); only the root-cause report is cited.
